<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/verify`, touching **63** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/verify/README.md`, `packages/verify/src/harness.ts`, `packages/verify/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**66** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8c1077615205d16e73fcbe77793d9ec428ff32e5`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/verify/README.md`, `packages/verify/src/harness.ts`, `packages/verify/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 37 pages)`, `master_detail (literal, 33 pages)`
- **33** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **30** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8c1077615205d16e73fcbe77793d9ec428ff32e5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d6c4be171d5a1c805ae160fd3d4a5ca89a69e3e6` — the merge of head `8b4a5802f071991f38272a0d7af9b29c9f76341d` into base `8c1077615205d16e73fcbe77793d9ec428ff32e5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d6c4be171d5a1c805ae160fd3d4a5ca89a69e3e6 && git checkout d6c4be171d5a1c805ae160fd3d4a5ca89a69e3e6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8c1077615205d16e73fcbe77793d9ec428ff32e5 8b4a5802f071991f38272a0d7af9b29c9f76341d && git checkout -B drift-repro 8c1077615205d16e73fcbe77793d9ec428ff32e5 && git merge --no-ff 8b4a5802f071991f38272a0d7af9b29c9f76341d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8c1077615205d16e73fcbe77793d9ec428ff32e5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8c1077615205d16e73fcbe77793d9ec428ff32e5` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8b4a5802f071991f38272a0d7af9b29c9f76341d`
Local-runs: none

Read at 2026-10-12T20:12Z, adversarially, against AGENTS.md Prime Directives #10 and #12 and Post-Task Checklist step 3. Inputs: card #15953 (body and all 19 comments: the classification table `6115219467` row 12, the slice 4 claim `6128881947` with slice 3's notes a-d, the dev report `6131548194`, the seat's ACCEPT `6131647524` read as a claim, and slice 3's record `6128105426` on PR #23069 as the precedent); PR #23091's body, file list and the net diff of `refs/pull/23091/head` against merge base `038d4c9588` (13 files, +1937 / -17, 14 commits including one merge of `origin/main`); the check-runs on the head, read four times. Nothing was built, run or re-run; the only local commands were `git fetch` / `git diff` / `git show` / `git log` against the fetched ref, the template print, `gh api` reads, and reads of untouched engine, REST, spec and harness files in the checkout for the seams the family names.

### ① Derived judgments

**The four functions and eleven types, reachable and coherent: right.** `packages/verify/package.json` maps `.` to `dist/index.js` / `dist/index.d.ts` (and the `require` pair); `packages/verify/src/index.ts` exports `deriveParentWriteReachCases`, `runParentWriteReachProofs`, `formatParentWriteReachReport`, `parentWriteReachSecurity` and exactly the eleven types the changeset lists from `./parent-write-reach.js`. The shapes follow the siblings: `deriveXCases(config)` / `runXProofs(stack, config)` / `formatXReport(report)`; `app` is the same expression; the six object statuses are slice 2's vocabulary with each docblock matching `objectStatus` and `judge` line for line. One deliberate difference, stated where it matters: `runParentWriteReachProofs` takes no caller token (it signs up every principal it writes as), and the README's API line and the changeset's signature say so. `summary.hardFailures` is `contradicted + failed` objects plus personas not run, a wider count than the sibling families' field count, and README, `cli.mdx` and the changeset each state the three terms. `parentWriteReachSecurity(config)` is `new SecurityPlugin({ ...appSecurityPluginOptions(config), defaultPermissionSets: [...securityDefaultPermissionSets, ...three sets] })`, the construction `rlsProbeSecurity` uses, so the app's declared default profile (`fallbackPermissionSet`) is carried, not dropped. What a stack gains when it is composed: three registered permission sets named `verify_parent_write_master_all` / `_detail_only` / `_no_delete`, authored over exactly the probed population (excluded and not-derivable cases are skipped) and inert until a `sys_user_permission_set` row names one (ADR-0131 D4), which only `runParentWriteReachProofs` writes; the plugin itself creates no principal. Confinement to a verify boot is by use and by the docs ("on a fresh stack of its own"), as it is for `rlsProbeSecurity`; nothing in the function refuses composition into a serving stack, and nothing in the sibling does either. Promises no more than measured.

**`os verify --parent-write-reach`: right.** `Flags.boolean` with `default: false`, typed into `runVerification`. With the flag, `bootStack(config, { multiTenant, hostRoot, security: parentWriteReachSecurity(config) })` is a fresh stack stopped in `finally`, the `--rls` pattern to the argument; `parentWriteReach.summary.hardFailures` is added under `?? 0`; the report rides `emitJson` (a `JSON.stringify`, so an `undefined` value emits no key); the text branch is `if (parentWriteReach)`. Without the flag nothing moves but help text (the description, one `examples` row, one flag), a widening the minor carries. `packages/cli/test/verify-parent-write-reach.test.ts` spawns the real process and pins it (`'parentWriteReach' in doc` false and exit 0 without the flag; exit 0 on the proven app; exit 1 on the hook-refused one).

**The expectation's source: right.** The population is `ObjectSchema.safeParse` (`sharingModel: 'controlled_by_parent'`, one `master_detail` read through `referenceCarrierOf`, whose real signature is `(def, reader)`), the chain walked through each master's own parse to the first master whose parse is not `controlled_by_parent`, the same predicate the engine's `declaresControlledByParent` applies at each hop. The detail half is `GET /auth/me/permissions` → `objects`, folded by the spec's `objectPermissionGrants(permission, target)`; that endpoint's `objects` slot is `buildEffectiveObjectPermissions`, the one function the server's own `current_user.can()` reads from (its #18783 note), so nothing is re-merged. The master half is `hooks.run(master, 'update', { id })` as the persona, which is `ql.update(master, { id }, { where: { id }, context })` through the engine's middleware chain: the object gate, the record gate and, for a master that is itself `controlled_by_parent`, `assertControlledByParentWrite`'s walk. The fixture pins the object gate (`detail-only` reads `not-editable` with the master's own `PERMISSION_DENIED`) and a `beforeUpdate` hook on the master (`pwc_frozen`); the record gate's refusal of an empty update is the dev's REST measurement, not pinned here, and nothing in the family depends on which gate refused. Grepped: the module resolves no sharing, ownership, hierarchy or chain; `owner_id` appears only as fixture stamping (who owns a seeded row) and `hasOwnerColumn` only decides whether an "own" chain can exist. The depth bound: `CHAIN_DEPTH_BOUND = 8` is sourced in its docblock to the amendment's "currently 8"; `CBP_MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH = 8` at `security-plugin.ts:515` is module-private, so the published value is the only honest source. The boundary is point-for-point: the engine denies when `++hops` reaches 8, i.e. eight `controlled_by_parent` masters above the detail, and the family excludes at `c.hops.length` reaching 8 after a `controlled_by_parent` master is pushed, i.e. the same eight; the derivation test pins `pwr_deep_1` (eight) excluded and `pwr_deep_2` (seven, eight hops) walked. A hand copy of a private constant is a drift hazard if the engine's bound ever moves; the remedy (an export from `plugin-security`) is outside this claim, and the docblock names the source, so it is a note. Every excluded shape is excluded, not modelled: no `master_detail` (the runtime's `resolveCbpRelation` third tier and the lint's `CBP_TIERS` third row both accept a required `lookup`; the family names that precedence in the reason and compares nothing), two `master_detail` fields (the engine picks by declaration order; not modelled), an undeclared master, a cycle, the bound, a parse refusal; not-derivable objects are named with the CRUD derivation's own reason.

**The door: equivalent where it matters, and the attribution is sound.** `hooks.run` with `{ as: token }` resolves the identity through `dispatcher.resolveRequestScope`, the same resolution a request gets, then calls `ql.insert(object, input, { context })`, `ql.update(object, { ...input, id }, { where: { id }, context })` and `ql.delete(object, { where: { id }, context })`. The REST data protocol (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` `createData` / `updateData` / `deleteData`) makes the same three engine calls with `where: { id: request.id }` and the request's context, so the security middleware and the bound hooks run identically on both. What a REST caller meets in addition is the HTTP layer's own concerns before the engine (route auth, exposure, body shaping) and the envelope after; none of them is ADR-0055 §3's verdict, and the report names its door `user` and the docs say "the insert, update and delete by id the REST data route makes". The dev's envelope measurement is confirmed in source: `classifyDataError`'s 403 arm (`@objectstack/types`, `data-error-classification.ts`) emits `{ code: 'PERMISSION_DENIED', object }` with `object` the ROUTE's argument and no `operation` and no `details`, and `PermissionDeniedError`'s own docblock rules `details` off the data wire (#7450); so a nested refusal on another object is unreadable at REST and the engine door is the right one for assumption 4. Attribution: `deniedFor` requires `code === 'PERMISSION_DENIED'`, `status === 403`, `details.object` the detail and `details.operation` the probed `update` / `delete` / `insert`; the engine's CRUD object-gate denial, the record-gate denial (`record_access_denied`) and the master-edit denial (`{ operation, object, recordId }`) all carry both, named for the caller's own object and operation as the amendment promises. Every other refusal is `unattributed`, a 5xx or a code-less throw is `failed`, a write answered written whose record does not show it is `not-run`, and a refusal whose record shows the write is `contradicted`; `write()` reads `status` then `statusCode`, both of which the error class carries. A hook refusing with the platform's envelope naming the detail is indistinguishable from the engine's refusal by design (it IS what the caller meets), which is what NEGATIVE CONTROL 1 relies on. Both ablations of `judge` red exactly their controls, as reported.

**The two-level pin: right, and the docs say the consequence.** The expectation on `pwr_quote_line` is the amendment's own sentence ("a detail whose whole chain is reachable stays readable and writable"): the persona's empty update of the quote is admitted and it holds every verb on the line, so `allowed`; the engine answers `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` "master not editable (row-level security)" from `assertMasterRowEditable` on the middle hop, and hotcrm's pinned 17.7.0 engine admits the same writes (run A, as reported). Pinning today's answer as `contradicted` in the family's own suite, with the flip condition in the test's comment, is the `--reference-shapes` precedent slice 1 set: the family is the measurement, the engine is outside the claim, and the fix to #23093 must update the pin or go red. #23093 is open, labelled `finding`, names the seam and the dedupe searches. README, `cli.mdx` and the changeset each state that an app declaring such a chain fails `--parent-write-reach` until then. Truthful.

**Carried note a: closes the residual, and the dev's remark holds.** `uniqueIndexesOver` reads the unique `indexes[]` entries covering the probed column from the declared object; `judge` returns `unattributed` on a field-less refusal where one exists, for insert and update, ahead of the twin rule. That is the first of the two tightenings `6128105426` named. The control (`uqc_item`: the field's own index blocked by the ADR-0120 D4 two-boot shape, a composite `[name, kind]` with `kind` defaulted) reads `inconclusive`, 4 of 4 `unattributed`, pinned with the detail text. The dispatch worded the exception as "unless a second twin varying that entry's other columns is admitted"; the dev's reading is the right one: a twin that keeps the probed value and varies the entry's other columns is ADMITTED exactly when the composite was the refuser (the field's own constraint is absent), and REFUSED when the field's own constraint holds, so only a refused second twin attributes the field. Not building it and reading `unattributed` is the safe direction, and the README, `cli.mdx` and the unreleased changeset state the narrower rule. The cost is stated too: a field that declares `unique` and also sits in any unique `indexes[]` entry now reads `inconclusive` on a field-less refusal, never `proven`.

**Notes b, c, d: right.** (b) six docblock lines on `bootStack` and one README paragraph say the config is `defineStack` output and what a raw literal costs; grounded, no behaviour change. (c) the README names the `auth.membership_policy` setting beside `OS_AUTH_MEMBERSHIP_POLICY`, both of which `plugin-auth` reads (verified on slice 3's record). (d) the changeset's and `cli.mdx`'s parenthetical now say `signUp`, then `POST /auth/organization/create`, which is `provisionOrganization`'s order.

**Docs sentences against the diff: right, with one stale comment.** Changeset: four functions, eleven types (counted against `index.ts`), the signature, the conjunction, the three verifier sets, the two chains and two detail owners, the attribution rule, the six statuses, `hardFailures`, the two-level sentence and the CLI paragraph all match `parent-write-reach.ts` and `verify.ts`. README: "Six app-agnostic proof families" (index.ts says six; the changeset says a sixth), the bullet, the opt-in paragraph, the exit-code sentence, the status table (each row matches `objectStatus`), the not-run paragraph (a persona whose answer names no set, `63d869dc02`) and the API line match. `cli.mdx`: the example row, the paragraph in the `os verify` section only, and the `--json` key list with `parentWriteReach` match. WRONG: the comment block above the new exports in `packages/verify/src/index.ts` says the conjunction is "asked of the engine through the REST door as verifier and declared-position personas"; the door is the engine's write as the persona, as the module header, README, `cli.mdx` and changeset all say. A sentence left from before `06ed55ddbe` moved the door. A source comment, not a published promise, so not a FAIL; owed a one-line fix on the next push to this file.

**The two `NOT_A_STAND_IN` rows: true of the code.** `runParentWriteReachProofs(stack: VerifyStack, config: any)` and `formatParentWriteReachReport(report: ParentWriteReachReport)` are exactly the gate's candidates (parameter 0 annotated with a package interface re-exported as a type); `VerifyStack` is the concrete handle `bootStack` returns and `ParentWriteReachReport` a value this package produced, so neither is a surface an out-of-tree implementer provides; the rows' words are the sibling rows' words. `deriveParentWriteReachCases(config: any)` and `parentWriteReachSecurity(config: any)` are not candidates. `Lint & Repo Gates`, which carries `check:verify-stand-in`, is green on the head.

**The fixture arithmetic is consistent.** 3 objects × 5 personas × 2 chains = 30 reaches, the rep's three chains another principal owns unreadable → 27 probed; 5 writes per reach → 135 = 54 + 54 + 27; the 31 contradictions on `pwr_quote_line` are exactly the expected-allowed probes (`master-all-records` 10, `master-all-records-no-delete` 6, `position:pwr_manager` 10, `position:pwr_rep` on its own chain 5); 104 held is the remainder. **First-consumer evidence (hotcrm):** read as reported, since no run was made here: row 12's D half holds with 0 contradictions on this tree's engine where the fixtures could be written, and the K residue (`sales_manager`'s grant) stays in hotcrm. The evidence came from direct runs of the family, not from `os verify`; see ③.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/15953-verify-parent-write-reach-family.md`: `@objectstack/verify` **minor**, `@objectstack/cli` **minor**. The diff publishes four new functions and eleven new types from `@objectstack/verify` and one new opt-in flag plus help text from `@objectstack/cli`; the only touched existing export, `runUniqueScopeProofs`, narrows what it will call `proven` (note a) in the safe direction and changes no signature, removes and renames nothing and changes no default. Minor is the right level for both and meets the card's own acceptance ("`@objectstack/verify` minor per new exported family"). Not breaking, so no migration text and no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed; the dev's `check-adr-0087-registration` reading ("adds no declared-breaking changeset") agrees.

`Clause-②` carriers: PR body line 2 `Clause-②: yes`; the changeset body `Clause-②: yes`; the claim comment `6128881947` `Clause-②: yes` (the bare form claim lines take). The three agree. Each is legal: `yes` with no arm is a complete declaration, and `yes` takes at least minor, which both entries are.

**The edit to slice 3's unreleased changeset** (`.changeset/15953-verify-unique-scope-family.md`, +2 / -2): the file landed on `main` in `f93bf12082` (PR #23069) and `.changeset/pre.json` is `{ mode: pre, tag: next }` with no consumed list, so no release has read it. The two sentences changed are the attribution rule (which this PR changes, note a) and the provisioning parenthetical (note d); the frontmatter levels are untouched. `check-empty-changeset` refuses the edit as its DELIBERATE CORRECTION class, which by the gate's own text stays red either way so that a person decides. The diff's truth supports **option A** (keep the corrected note): after this PR the base's sentence ("it names none and the same record with only the probed value changed is admitted" credits the field) is false where a unique `indexes[]` entry covers the field; the note is unreleased and the same card's, so the CHANGELOG entry that ships is the corrected one; option B would ship the sentence this PR falsified beside its erratum in the same release. ⛔ The decision is the maintainer's; the gate stays red until that confirmation, and the queue cannot take the PR before it.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report `6131548194`: one `open_questions` entry (the changeset correction), answered in ② as a maintainer decision with the option the diff supports. Its deviations and findings, each answered or escalated:

- **The door** (assumption 5): answered in ① — the same three engine calls the REST data protocol makes, the identity resolved the same way, the REST envelope confirmed in source to name the route's object and no operation.
- **The detail half from effective permissions** (assumption 2): answered in ① — the one merge the server itself reads from; a second copy is what ADR-0124 D4 refuses.
- **The verifier personas** (assumption 3): the sets live in the registry (`defaultPermissionSets`), the grant row names one through the seed door, and the server's `permissionSets` answer is checked before the persona is used; a stack booted without the plugin reports them not run with the remedy and counts them, pinned. The position personas reuse `provisionRlsPositionPersona` and `declaredPositionNames` verbatim. Answered.
- **The depth bound**: answered in ① — sourced to the amendment, point-for-point today, a drift hazard if the private constant moves; a note.
- **The pinned two-level answer**: answered in ① — #23093 is the carrier, and it is open.
- **Conditional surfaces**: two `NOT_A_STAND_IN` rows (the gate asked); the `#22661` `CALLERS` row not needed — the module imports no `referenceTargetOf` (its imports are `ObjectSchema`, `referenceCarrierOf`, `objectPermissionGrants`, the three `plugin-security` names, `declaredCollection`, the two CRUD helpers and the two RLS helpers). Answered.
- **One merge of `origin/main`**: the head is four commits past it, no force-push, the net diff is the 13 files reviewed. Answered.
- **hotcrm evidence by direct runs, with the artifact's 76 `email_template.category` tombstones removed in memory**: this tree is protocol 18 and hotcrm pins `^17.7.0`, so the card's clause "runs from `os verify` on hotcrm's metadata" cannot be met on this tree for this slice either; the in-memory removal is an adaptation of the evidence run's input, not of the family. ESCALATED, not a FAIL: the same open acceptance note slices 1, 2 and 3 landed under (`6116484972`, `6124307791`, `6128501535`); the card stays open for its remaining rows, and whoever closes it owes that clause a run or a re-scope.
- **Commit trailers and local leftovers**: process notes, not contract matters. Answered.
- **Out-of-scope finding 1** (the two-level refusal): filed as #23093 by the seat; the family's test pins it. Answered.
- **Finding 2, carrier none — the runtime and the lint accept a required `lookup` as a `controlled_by_parent` master, which ADR-0055 §1 and the spec's `sharingModel` docblock do not state.** NEEDS A CARRIER. ADR-0055 §1 reads "must declare exactly one required `master_detail` field ... Validation error otherwise (fail closed)"; `resolveCbpRelation`'s third tier (`pick(lookup && required)`) and the lint's `CBP_TIERS` third row (#7503 / #14747, "the runtime's winner, exactly") both derive through a required lookup, and the spec's `safeParse` accepts an object with no `master_detail` and one with two (the derivation test's `pwr_no_master` and `pwr_two_masters` both parse). That is an accepted ADR's §1 enforced by neither the parse nor the runtime, and a runtime widening no ADR records: Prime Directive #13 (an accepted ADR binds until a superseding record says otherwise) and #10 (a contract violation gets an issue) put a carrier on it, whichever way it resolves (an amendment recording the tier, or its retirement, with the lint following). Not this PR's defect: the family stays on the ADR's side and excludes those objects with the reason (hotcrm's `crm_campaign_member`, `crm_event_attendee`, `crm_article_feedback`), so this does not move the head. ESCALATED: the seat owes the card; lane and grade are triage's.
- **Finding 3, carrier none — the REST envelope names the route's object and carries no operation on every refusal.** A note is right: `classifyDataError`'s 403 arm is deliberate and `PermissionDeniedError` rules `details` off the data wire by a recorded ruling (#7450); the family's choice of door is the consequence, and this record confirms it in source. No carrier.
- **Finding 4, carrier none — a generic fixture cannot satisfy every app rule** (hotcrm's `contract_validation`): reported `inconclusive` with the app's own refusal, never `proven`; slice 3's finding 4 was the same class. A note is right. No carrier.
- **Finding 5, carrier none — `fixtureBody` and its helpers copied in three family modules**: a refactor into `derive.ts`, outside this claim; not a defect under #10. A note is right; a later slice of this card may fold it.
- **Finding 6, carrier none — `provisionRlsPositionPersona` writes "minted by `objectstack verify --rls`" on the position row whichever family calls it**: cosmetic, on ephemeral stacks only; a one-word parameter in a later slice. A note is right. No carrier.
- **Added by this review**: the stale "through the REST door" comment in `packages/verify/src/index.ts` (①), owed a one-line fix on the next push to this file; not a carrier.

**Check-runs on the head, read four times in this act, the last at 20:12Z (latest run per name).** At the final read every run had concluded: 32 success, 7 skipped, 1 failure, 0 in progress.
